data.summary: The theme feature is well structured: the logic is testable and injectable, the no-flash script is present, the header uses boxed links, and Tailwind uses darkMode 'class'. However, Header renders two ThemeToggle instances (desktop and mobile) that do not stay in sync. The 'themeChanged' event is dispatched but nothing listens to it, so the other toggle shows a stale preference and icon. Charts are also not themed for dark mode. The diff was partly truncated, so the dark variants in the investment components were not fully reviewed.

findings.issue: Header renders two ThemeToggle instances (desktop and mobile), each holding its own `preference` state. setTheme dispatches 'themeChanged' but no component listens to it. After choosing Dark in one instance, the other still shows the old icon and aria-label. If that stale instance was on 'system', its OS-change listener still re-applies 'system' and can override the user's explicit choice when the OS preference flips.
findings.suggestion: Subscribe to THEME_CHANGE_EVENT in a useEffect and call setPreference(event.detail). Also listen to the 'storage' event for cross-tab sync. Alternatively, drop the unused event if it is not needed.
findings.rule: Acceptance criteria: System mode reacts to OS changes correctly

findings.issue: THEME_CHANGE_EVENT is dispatched with no consumer, so it is effectively dead code. The dispatch branch in setTheme is also untested.
findings.suggestion: Consume it in ThemeToggle (see the MAJOR finding) and add a test that setTheme dispatches the event, or remove it.

findings.issue: The ThemeToggle component and the system-change subscription have no tests. The 'preference follows OS change without reload' criterion is only covered indirectly through applyTheme.
findings.suggestion: Extract a subscribeToSystemTheme(matchMedia, doc, onChange) helper into lib/theme.js and unit-test it with an injected matchMedia that fires the change listener.
findings.rule: AGENTS.md: comprehensive tests for new classes

findings.issue: The dark-mode criterion says there should be no unreadable text, but chart colors are not themed (reported as a follow-up). Axis and label text in ApexCharts/Recharts may be dark on a dark card.
findings.suggestion: Pass the resolved theme to the chart options, or at least set light label colors under dark mode, before declaring the criterion met.

architectureNotes: Theme logic is isolated in lib/theme.js with injectable storage, document and matchMedia, which keeps it unit-testable under node:test.
The inline script in Layout duplicates the resolution logic from theme.js. This is acceptable for no-flash, but keep the two in sync.
positives: No-flash inline script with try/catch around localStorage.
getStoredTheme and setTheme degrade gracefully when storage is unavailable.
Header link classes are factored into shared constants instead of four copies of the duplicated conditional.
The ThemeToggle menu has proper ARIA roles and handles Escape and outside-click.
Tests inject all globals and no existing tests were weakened.
mustFixBeforeMerge: Make multiple ThemeToggle instances stay in sync: listen to THEME_CHANGE_EVENT (and 'storage') in ThemeToggle and update `preference`, so a stale instance cannot show a wrong icon or re-apply 'system'.
